message: I hear what you are saying about student motivation by evaluation. I see it in my students as well. I am curious about how rigid ( if that's the right word) students can be about needing, expecting and privileging evaluation over non-evaluation. If I don't grade it ("revise" as they say), it's not worth anything.  and it relates to the non-process behavior, where revision is viewed as busywork or as something that the instructor must supervise.  I feel that writing on the lower levels has become so mind numbingly structured and supervised that students are almost hard-wired to expect writing classes to be boring etc. etc. but it's nearly midnight during exam week, and I'm wandering into the tangential. Happy Birthday to T and Z, and post a pic of them, okay?
